display.title: Tanya Chapter 36, Part 1: Light from Darkness, the Purpose of Creation
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur on chapter 36: this lowest world is the goal of all creation, where turning darkness into light brings Hashem the deepest pleasure.
display.summary_long: A class in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series on Tanya chapter 36, beginning in the middle of the lesson. The chain of worlds shows that no higher world is a goal in itself; the purpose of all of them is this lowest, physical world, which is compared to a factory whose finished product is what everything was built for. Here, where darkness and challenges hide Hashem, a Jew who subdues the 'other side' and turns darkness into light brings Hashem a pleasure the higher worlds cannot give, like the dazzling light that greets someone stepping out of a dark room. A practical digression explains guarding one's thoughts: a stray thought that falls into the mind is not a person's fault, but entertaining it is, which is why the Shulchan Aruch begins with 'I place Hashem before me always'. The class then asks how a created being could bear Hashem's infinite light without ceasing to exist. The answer is the Torah, called 'oz', strength: it prepares the soul to receive the revelation of the days of Moshiach, when the light of Hashem will be seen openly and the sun will no longer be needed.
display.lesson: This world is the goal of all creation; every time we overcome the yetzer hara and bring light into darkness we give Hashem true pleasure, and our Torah and mitzvos give us the strength to receive the light of Moshiach.
